name: Oklo Inc.
employees: 205 full-time in the US across 33 states plus 2 in Canada (31 December 2025)
summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: Oklo is a pre-commercial advanced-fission developer building its first 75 MWe sodium-cooled fast reactor at Idaho National Laboratory under a Department of Energy authorization pathway rather than an NRC licence, funded by roughly $3.0B of raised capital against an order book composed almost entirely of non-binding instruments; the first Aurora powerhouse is targeted for late 2027 to early 2028 and no Aurora has ever produced power. BACKGROUND. Founded 2013 by Jacob and Caroline DeWitte; listed on the NYSE 10 May 2024 through a merger with AltC Acquisition Corp. that delivered about $306M of gross proceeds. The company intends to build, own and operate its plants and sell electricity and heat under long-term power purchase agreements rather than sell reactors. Three business lines: the Aurora powerhouse, a fuel line (an Aurora Fuel Fabrication Facility at INL and an announced recycling facility in Tennessee), and radioisotopes through the wholly owned subsidiary Atomic Alchemy. FY2025 net loss was $105.7M on no revenue at all; the first revenue in company history — $1.210M — was recognised in the quarter ended 30 June 2026 and came from engineering, consulting and fabrication services acquired in 2026, not from power. Collection gap: the company publishes no levelised cost of energy, no thermal rating for the 15-75 MWe class, and no HALEU enrichment percentage.
ecosystemRole: The most-named advanced-fission vendor inside this corpus and the clearest test of whether an AI campus can buy clean firm power from a company that has never sold any. Oklo sits on the generation side of the fence rather than inside the building: it appears in Switch's dossier as a 12 GW non-binding master agreement, in Equinix's as the first colocation SMR deal, in Meta's as up to 1.2 GW of a January 2026 nuclear package, and in Kiewit's as the constructor seat on the first unit. Its supply chain reaches back into companies already covered here — Siemens Energy for the power conversion system under the only binding commercial contract Oklo has announced, Kiewit for construction, Vertiv for power and thermal reference designs, ABB for the operator monitoring room, and NVIDIA with Los Alamos for fuel-modelling work. The dossier's value is therefore less as a supplier profile than as a calibration exercise: it is the file where the distinction between an announcement, a licensing milestone and a delivered megawatt-hour has to be held most carefully.

productsAndServices.name: Aurora powerhouse — sodium-cooled fast reactor
productsAndServices.description: A liquid-metal-cooled, metal-fuelled fast reactor built on the design and operating heritage of Experimental Breeder Reactor II, which ran at Idaho from 1964 to 1994. Company materials describe the product line as designed to produce 15 to 75 MWe with the potential to expand powerhouse size to 100 MWe and higher. Power conversion is a steam Rankine cycle: Siemens Energy is under binding contract to deliver a condensing SST-600 steam turbine, an SGen-100A industrial generator and associated auxiliaries for the first unit. Refuelling is stated at approximately 2,500 kg roughly every ten years across a 40-year plant design life. No Aurora is operating; the first, Aurora-INL at 75 MWe, broke ground on 22 September 2025 and is under construction.
highlights: Aurora-INL is rated 75 MWe. The Eielson Air Force Base unit named in the June 2025 notice of intent to award is rated 5 MWe plus 60 MWth — the only thermal rating Oklo publishes anywhere

Design lineage caution, from Oklo's own record: the Aurora announced in December 2019 was a ~1.5 MWe heat-pipe machine, and the 2020 combined licence application the NRC accepted and later denied was for that design. The current Aurora is a 15-75 MWe sodium-cooled steam-cycle plant. Same product name, materially different machine

Modularity is transport-based rather than whole-reactor factory assembly: company materials state all components can be transported by truck and lifted by typical cranes, and that minimal site preparation is expected before installation

Safety claim, company wording: the reactor is 'self-stabilizing, self-controlling, and cooled by natural forces… the plant is walk-away safe'. Oklo cites over 400 reactor-years of worldwide operating experience for liquid-metal-cooled metal-fuelled fast reactors
Air-cooled condensers: company materials state one Aurora powerhouse uses about 9,000 gallons of water a day, or 5 gallons per MWh, and does not need siting next to a body of water

Automation is a licensing strategy as well as an operations one — the company states it is designing reactors to be largely automated to minimise the number of individually NRC-licensed human operators, and has a Licensed Operator topical report under NRC review proposing to license operators to the technology rather than to a single site
Collection gap: no MWth rating is published for the 15 or 75 MWe class, and no HALEU enrichment percentage or range appears in any first-party source
productsAndServices.positioning: Differentiated within the advanced-reactor set on three axes at once, per independent tracking: a fast neutron spectrum where NuScale, GE Hitachi and Holtec are light-water designs; a build-own-operate commercial model where the rest of the field sells reactors to utilities; and a first unit proceeding under DOE authorization where NuScale holds a standard design approval, TerraPower and Kairos hold NRC construction permits, and X-energy and Holtec have construction permit applications under review. Oklo holds no NRC reactor licence and, as of the Q2 2026 filing, no docketed reactor application.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct. The company designs, builds, owns and operates and sells the output; it states its primary business model is to sell energy through PPAs as opposed to selling powerhouse designs, while noting it intends to offer customers flexibility in business model as the technology matures.
productsAndServices.roadmap: Aurora-INL commercial operations targeted late 2027 to early 2028 (the FY2025 10-K states the broader target of deploying the first powerhouse in 2028). Aurora-Ohio: pre-construction and site characterisation slated to begin 2026, first phase targeted as early as 2030, expanding to 1.2 GW by 2034.

productsAndServices.name: Fuel line — Aurora Fuel Fabrication Facility and the Tennessee recycling facility
productsAndServices.description: A vertically integrated fuel programme in two parts. The Aurora Fuel Fabrication Facility (A3F) at Idaho National Laboratory will fabricate metal fuel from used EBR-II material recycled by INL; DOE approved its Safety Design Strategy (January 2024), Conceptual Safety Design Report (October 2024), Nuclear Safety Design Agreement (November 2025) and Preliminary Documented Safety Analysis (December 2025), and fabrication equipment has entered manufacturing for installation and startup in 2027. Separately, Oklo announced in September 2025 a fuel recycling facility in Oak Ridge, Tennessee as the first phase of an advanced fuel centre with investment totalling up to $1.68B and more than 800 stated jobs; it is in NRC pre-application engagement with civil engineering and site-grading permitting underway.
highlights: The first core comes from a 2019-2020 award: five metric tons of HALEU produced from recovered uranium from previously irradiated EBR-II fuel at INL, following INL's selection of Oklo in February 2020

Commercial HALEU is a letter of intent, not a contract. Centrus agreed in June 2026 to supply enough domestic HALEU for up to five Aurora powerhouses with deliveries scheduled to begin in 2029, from the American Centrifuge Plant in Pike County, Ohio. The Q2 2026 filing states timing, volume, pricing and prepayment terms 'remain subject to further negotiation and the execution of a definitive agreement'

A separate Centrus joint venture for HALEU deconversion at Piketon is at the discussions stage — the March 2026 release states the companies 'have agreed to pursue discussions regarding a joint venture'

The recycling technology is non-separative: company materials describe advanced techniques that keep transuranic materials together and 'do not create pure material streams'. Oklo states it has won over $15M in DOE recycling awards and completed a first end-to-end demonstration with Argonne and INL in July 2024

A third fuel pathway is in negotiation: Oklo was selected by DOE for advanced negotiations under the Surplus Plutonium Utilization Program (May 2026), supported by a fast-spectrum plutonium criticality experiment run with Los Alamos in December 2025

Company framing of the risk, verbatim from the FY2025 10-K: 'The cost environment for various sources of fuel (including HALEU) has increased significantly in recent years, which is why we are implementing a diversified fuel strategy'
productsAndServices.positioning: Vertical integration into fuel is the structural feature that distinguishes Oklo from every peer in the advanced-reactor set and the reason it has revenue and an operating reactor while having no operating power plant. Independent reporting places the industry constraint plainly: US HALEU enrichment is at pilot scale, and DOE's first HALEU allocation round in April 2025 went to five developers that did not include Oklo — Oklo's fuel comes instead from the older INL EBR-II route, and DOE retains ownership of that material.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Internal supply in the first instance; the Tennessee facility is described as also serving external customers, and a non-binding MOU with Standard Nuclear covers potential purchases of recycled fuel materials.
productsAndServices.roadmap: A3F equipment installation and startup 2027. Tennessee recycling facility expected to begin producing metal fuel for Aurora powerhouses by the early 2030s.

productsAndServices.name: Atomic Alchemy — radioisotopes and the Groves test reactor
productsAndServices.description: A wholly owned subsidiary acquired on 28 February 2025 for consideration of approximately $28.4M, developing US radioisotope production for healthcare, industry, research and defence around a proprietary Versatile Isotope Production Reactor (VIPR) design. The Groves Isotope Test Reactor at Lockhart, Texas broke ground on 3 September 2025 and achieved first criticality on 5 August 2026 under a DOE Other Transaction Agreement within the Reactor Pilot Program — the first and so far only Oklo-built reactor to operate. A separate Idaho Radiochemistry Laboratory received an NRC materials licence on 17 March 2026, Oklo's first NRC-issued licence of any kind.
highlights: Groves is NOT an Aurora and NOT a power reactor. The planned VIPR family is described as light-water-cooled, pool-type units of around 15 MWth each, up to four in an Idaho isotope foundry — a different machine from the sodium-cooled fast Aurora

Build metric, company wording: 'Substantial construction was completed in 229 days, representing, to our knowledge, the fastest privately funded and privately sited nuclear reactor build in history' — greenfield to operational in just over eleven months, and the first Reactor Pilot Program reactor to reach criticality on private rather than government land

The March 2026 NRC materials licence authorises receipt, possession, use, storage, processing, repackaging, manufacture and distribution of up to 2 curies of radium-226 plus sealed cobalt-60 and americium-241 sources, and the company states it enables initial commercial sales

Atomic Alchemy withdrew its previously submitted NRC construction permit application for the Meitner-1 commercial radioisotope facility at INL in January 2026 to focus on the Radioisotope Pilot Facility

Revenue disclosure caution: the FY2025 10-K states the consolidated statements include no revenue and an immaterial loss from operations for Atomic Alchemy. The Q2 2026 revenue disaggregation shows engineering and consulting $800K, manufacturing and fabrication $168K and 'Other' $242K — isotope sales are not separately labelled
productsAndServices.positioning: The only advanced-reactor developer in the covered set with a revenue-adjacent, near-term, non-power nuclear business. It is why 'Oklo has an operating reactor' and 'no Aurora has produced power' are both true statements about the same company at the same time.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct sales of isotopes; the Idaho materials licence is the instrument that permits distribution.
productsAndServices.roadmap: Idaho multi-reactor isotope foundry with up to four VIPR systems, stage described as under development.

productsAndServices.name: Manufacturing and engineering services (ARMEC, Creative Engineers)
productsAndServices.description: Two 2026 acquisitions that brought Oklo its first revenue. ARMEC (announced 8 June 2026) adds manufacturing and prototyping capability; Creative Engineers (announced 30 June 2026) adds roughly thirty years of specialised engineering and fabrication experience in alkali-metal systems, including sodium-related components — directly relevant to a sodium-cooled reactor. The company states both generate positive free cash flow. Together they contributed $968K of revenue and a $42K net loss in the quarter ended 30 June 2026.
highlights: This is the entire origin of Oklo's revenue. Total revenue recognised in Q2 2026 was $1.210M, disaggregated as engineering and consulting services $800K, manufacturing and fabrication services $168K, and other $242K
Revenue was $0 for FY2024, $0 for FY2025 and $0 for Q1 2026 — the FY2025 10-K income statement carries no revenue line at all and opens directly with operating expenses
The Creative Engineers acquisition is a supply-chain hedge as much as a capability purchase: alkali-metal component fabrication is a narrow speciality and the Aurora depends on it
productsAndServices.positioning: A vertical-integration move consistent with the fuel programme: bringing scarce, schedule-critical capabilities in-house rather than contracting for them.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct engineering and fabrication services to third parties, alongside internal work.

recentDevelopments.headline: PJM withdraws Oklo's 750 MW Pike County interconnection project; Oklo files an emergency complaint at FERC
recentDevelopments.read: The interconnection, not the reactor, is the binding constraint on the Meta-backed Ohio campus — and Oklo says the withdrawal costs it at least 14 months.
recentDevelopments.source: Utility Dive — PJM drops Oklo advanced nuclear project from interconnection study cycle (published 2026-08-31, updated 2026-09-01)

recentDevelopments.headline: Q2 2026: first revenue in company history at $1.210M, net loss $48.5M, cash and marketable securities $3.006B; 2026 spending guidance raised
recentDevelopments.read: Revenue arrived from acquired engineering and fabrication services rather than from power, and the guidance raise says the build is accelerating rather than the plan changing.

recentDevelopments.headline: Groves Isotope Test Reactor achieves first criticality on 5 August 2026 — the first Oklo-built reactor to operate, and not an Aurora
recentDevelopments.read: A genuine milestone that proves the DOE authorization pathway end to end, on a light-water pool-type isotope reactor that shares no reactor technology with the Aurora.

recentDevelopments.headline: DOE grants startup authorization for the Groves reactor, clearing fuel loading and first criticality
recentDevelopments.read: The final rung of the five-step DOE ladder, reached on a privately sited reactor — the template Oklo intends to repeat at Idaho.

recentDevelopments.headline: Acquires Creative Engineers, adding roughly thirty years of alkali-metal systems engineering including sodium-related components
recentDevelopments.read: A supply-chain hedge on the narrowest speciality the Aurora depends on, bought rather than contracted for.

recentDevelopments.headline: Letter of intent with Centrus for HALEU sufficient for up to five Aurora powerhouses, deliveries scheduled to begin 2029; Kiewit MOU for Ohio EPC planning
recentDevelopments.read: The commercial fuel supply is still a letter of intent whose price, volume and prepayment terms are all unnegotiated — three years before the first delivery date.

recentDevelopments.headline: DOE approves the Preliminary Documented Safety Analysis for Aurora-INL
recentDevelopments.read: Third of five rungs on the DOE ladder for the first power reactor; the Documented Safety Analysis, readiness review and startup authorization all remain ahead.

recentDevelopments.headline: Acquires ARMEC for manufacturing and prototyping capability; company states it generates positive free cash flow
recentDevelopments.read: Together with Creative Engineers this is the entire source of the company's first revenue.

recentDevelopments.headline: Selected by DOE for advanced negotiations under the Surplus Plutonium Utilization Program
recentDevelopments.read: A third fuel pathway beside the EBR-II legacy stock and the Centrus letter of intent, and the one most exposed to security and safeguards conditions.

recentDevelopments.headline: NRC approves Oklo's Principal Design Criteria topical report for the Aurora, 'in less than half the traditional review timeline'
recentDevelopments.read: Real NRC progress on a component of a future application, which does not change the fact that no reactor application is docketed.

recentDevelopments.headline: Collaboration with NVIDIA and Los Alamos National Laboratory on AI-enabled modelling, digital twins and fuel validation for plutonium-bearing fuels
recentDevelopments.read: The AI-and-nuclear relationship running in the unusual direction: compute applied to fuel qualification rather than reactors applied to compute.

recentDevelopments.headline: Four directors appointed effective 10 April 2026; Michael Thompson named Lead Independent Director; CTO Pat Schweiger to transition to senior technical advisor
recentDevelopments.read: A governance strengthening that partly answers the combined chair-and-chief-executive role, alongside the departure of the chief technical officer from an operating seat at a first-of-a-kind engineering company.

recentDevelopments.headline: DOE signs the Other Transaction Agreement and approves the Nuclear Safety Design Agreement for Aurora-INL; Atomic Alchemy granted an NRC materials licence
recentDevelopments.read: Two different regulators on the same day — the DOE clearing the reactor's path and the NRC granting Oklo its first licence of any kind, for two curies of radium.

recentDevelopments.headline: Oklo and Centrus announce a planned joint venture to advance nuclear fuel services in Ohio
recentDevelopments.read: Announced at the discussions stage — the release states the companies 'have agreed to pursue discussions regarding a joint venture'.

recentDevelopments.headline: Meta prepayment agreement supporting a 1.2 GW clean-energy campus in Pike County, Ohio; first phase targeted as early as 2030
recentDevelopments.read: The strongest instrument in the customer book — Meta's funding secures fuel rather than merely expressing intent — and its interconnection was withdrawn by PJM seven months later.

recentDevelopments.headline: DOE Other Transaction Agreement for the Radioisotope Pilot Facility; Atomic Alchemy withdraws its NRC construction permit application for Meitner-1
recentDevelopments.read: A deliberate move off the NRC track and onto the DOE track for the isotope programme as well as the power programme.

recentDevelopments.headline: Binding contract with Siemens Energy for the Aurora-INL power conversion system: a condensing SST-600 steam turbine and SGen-100A generator
recentDevelopments.read: The only binding commercial contract in the entire company record, and it is with a supplier rather than a customer.

recentDevelopments.headline: Groundbreaking on the first Aurora powerhouse at Idaho National Laboratory — a 75 MWe sodium-cooled fast reactor on EBR-II heritage
recentDevelopments.read: Construction of the first unit is genuinely under way; commissioning is targeted for late 2027 to early 2028 under DOE authorization rather than an NRC licence.

recentDevelopments.headline: Announces a fuel recycling facility in Oak Ridge, Tennessee as the first phase of an advanced fuel centre worth up to $1.68B and more than 800 jobs
recentDevelopments.read: The largest single capital commitment the company has announced, and it is a fuel plant rather than a power plant — the clearest statement of where Oklo thinks the bottleneck is.

recentDevelopments.headline: Oklo and Atomic Alchemy selected for three of eleven projects under the DOE Reactor Pilot Program
recentDevelopments.read: The decision that reshaped the schedule: a route to construct and operate that does not require an NRC reactor licence first.

recentDevelopments.headline: Strategic alliance with Liberty Energy pairing gas bridge power with later nuclear baseload; Liberty had committed $10M to Oklo in 2023
recentDevelopments.read: An honest acknowledgement of the gap: the near-term product for a data-centre customer is gas, with the reactor arriving years later.

recentDevelopments.headline: Collaboration agreement with Vertiv to co-develop power and thermal reference designs, with a pilot demonstration planned for the first Aurora
recentDevelopments.read: Positions the reactor inside the data-centre equipment stack rather than beside it — the same reference-design pattern the cooling and power OEMs use with NVIDIA.

recentDevelopments.headline: Kiewit Nuclear Solutions selected as lead constructor for the first Aurora powerhouse under a Master Services Agreement
recentDevelopments.read: Buys execution credibility from a contractor with a completed HVDC delivery and an 11 GW gas book, on non-nuclear scope.

recentDevelopments.headline: Defense Logistics Agency Energy issues a Notice of Intent to Award for a 5 MWe plus 60 MWth powerhouse at Eielson Air Force Base, Alaska
recentDevelopments.read: A notice of intent rather than an award, and independent reporting states it is conditional on Oklo obtaining an NRC licence — which it does not hold.

recentDevelopments.headline: Sam Altman steps down as chairman; CEO Jacob DeWitte becomes chairman
recentDevelopments.read: Removes a conflict ahead of possible AI-company supply talks and combines the chair and chief-executive roles in one person; no OpenAI agreement has followed in the seventeen months since.

recentDevelopments.headline: Closes the acquisition of radioisotope developer Atomic Alchemy for consideration of approximately $28.4M
recentDevelopments.read: Bought the business that would put an Oklo-built reactor into operation eighteen months later — on a completely different reactor technology.

recentDevelopments.headline: Chris Wright steps down from the board on confirmation as US Secretary of Energy
recentDevelopments.read: A director moving to run the department that would, four months later, create the authorization pathway Oklo's first reactor now uses.

recentDevelopments.headline: Non-binding master power agreement with Switch for 12 GW of Aurora capacity through 2044
recentDevelopments.read: Twelve of the fourteen gigawatts Oklo went on to describe as an order book sit in this single non-binding instrument; individual binding agreements are to be finalised as project milestones are reached.

recentDevelopments.headline: Letters of intent with two unnamed data-centre providers for up to 750 MW, taking the stated pipeline to approximately 2,100 MW
recentDevelopments.read: The pipeline grew by announcement rather than by contract; Oklo stopped publishing a pipeline figure after mid-2025.

recentDevelopments.headline: Non-binding letter of intent with Wyoming Hyperscale (now Prometheus Hyperscale) covering an intended 20-year, 100 MW power purchase agreement
recentDevelopments.read: Two years on, no conversion to a definitive agreement has been reported.

recentDevelopments.headline: Begins trading on the NYSE as OKLO following the merger with AltC Acquisition Corp., with approximately $306M of gross proceeds
recentDevelopments.read: The listing that funded everything since; three subsequent at-the-market programmes have raised roughly six times as much again.

recentDevelopments.headline: Non-binding letter of intent with Diamondback Energy for 50 MW over 20 years in the Permian Basin
recentDevelopments.read: The only oil-and-gas counterparty in the book, and non-binding like the rest.

recentDevelopments.headline: NRC denies Oklo's combined licence application without prejudice for failure to supply information
recentDevelopments.read: The denial that reshaped the strategy: Oklo has held no docketed NRC reactor application since, and its first plant is proceeding under DOE authorization instead.
recentDevelopments.source: NRC news release 22-002 and denial letter ML21357A034, 2022-01-06

relationships.note: Under binding contract to deliver the Aurora-INL power conversion system — the only binding commercial contract in Oklo's public record.
relationships.context:
The relationship ran through three escalating instruments: a memorandum of understanding in December 2023, a preferred-supplier agreement in August 2024, and a binding contract signed on 19 November 2025 covering a condensing SST-600 steam turbine, an SGen-100A industrial generator and associated auxiliaries.

It is the single most useful fact about the Aurora's architecture. A sodium-cooled fast reactor is exotic on the nuclear side and entirely conventional on the power side: the secondary circuit is a steam Rankine cycle, and the turbine and generator can therefore be bought from an established turbine OEM rather than developed. Siemens Energy's own dossier here covers that catalogue from the other direction.

relationships.note: Lead constructor for the first Aurora powerhouse under a Master Services Agreement, with a separate MOU covering Ohio EPC planning.
relationships.context:
Kiewit Nuclear Solutions was selected on 15 July 2025 as lead constructor for Aurora-INL, focused on non-nuclear scope, and a memorandum of understanding covering engineering, procurement and construction planning for the Ohio campus followed on 18 June 2026. Groundbreaking at Idaho took place on 22 September 2025.

Kiewit's own dossier records the seat and its scale — roughly 370 construction jobs, commissioning targeted late 2027 to early 2028 — and notes as a negative finding that no confirmed Kiewit role exists on TerraPower Natrium, BWXT or X-energy programmes. The Oklo seat is the verified advanced-reactor relationship on both sides.

relationships.note: Non-binding master power agreement — a framework, with individual binding agreements to be finalised as project milestones are reached.
relationships.context:
Signed 18 December 2024 and described by both parties as one of the largest corporate clean-power agreements ever signed. It is explicitly non-binding: the master agreement establishes a framework, and Switch's own dossier records the same caution — 'non-binding, with no operating Oklo plant yet'.

Its significance is arithmetic as much as commercial. Oklo's stated order book reached approximately 14 GW after this signing, which means roughly six sevenths of the pipeline sits inside this one instrument. Oklo stopped publishing a pipeline figure after mid-2025.

relationships.note: Prepayment agreement supporting the Pike County, Ohio campus — Meta prepays for power and funds powerhouse deployment; Oklo states the funding secures nuclear fuel.
relationships.context:
Announced 9 January 2026 and signed on 5 January. It is the strongest instrument in Oklo's customer book because it moves money rather than intent: Meta prepays for power and the funding is applied to securing fuel for the first phase. Neither the dollar value nor the bindingness of the whole agreement is disclosed, and it is not described as a power purchase agreement.

Meta's own dossier records it inside a January 2026 nuclear package of up to 6.6 GW alongside TerraPower and Vistra, with the Oklo element at up to 1.2 GW targeted for around 2030. The campus interconnection was withdrawn by PJM on 3 August 2026 and is under emergency complaint at FERC.

relationships.note: Non-binding letters of intent with a $25M prepayment and a right of first refusal, reported as the first colocation-operator SMR deal.
relationships.context:
The letter of intent was executed on 16 February 2024 and disclosed in an AltC SEC filing on 2 April 2024. Independent reporting describes a $25M prepayment and a right of first refusal on 100 to 500 MWe for up to 36 months — a window that expires around February 2027. Oklo names Equinix among its LOI counterparties in the FY2025 10-K but has never issued a dedicated release.

Equinix's own dossier records it as the first data-centre-operator SMR deal at 500 MW, inside the most diversified firm-power book in colocation, beside Bloom fuel cells, Radiant, Rolls-Royce SMR and Stellaria.
relationships.source: Oklo FY2025 Form 10-K (LOI counterparties named); Data Center Dynamics — Equinix signs deal for up to 500MW, makes $25m pre-payment (2024-04)

relationships.note: Collaboration agreement to co-develop power and thermal reference designs for hyperscale and colocation data centres, with a pilot demonstration planned for the first Aurora.
relationships.context:
Announced 22 July 2025. It is a technology collaboration rather than a power offtake: the two companies intend to publish integrated reference designs so that a campus can be engineered around an Aurora from the outset rather than retrofitted to one.

The pattern is the same one the cooling and power OEMs use with NVIDIA — sell the blueprint before the hardware — applied here to generation. Vertiv's own guide in this app teaches the thermal chain and the UPS the reference design would have to accommodate.

relationships.note: Collaboration with NVIDIA and Los Alamos National Laboratory on AI-enabled modelling, digital twins and fuel validation for plutonium-bearing fuels.
relationships.context:
Announced 23 April 2026. Unusually for this corpus, the compute is pointed at the reactor rather than the reactor at the compute: the work applies AI-enabled modelling and digital twins to fuel qualification, supporting the surplus-plutonium pathway Oklo entered advanced negotiations on a month later.

A separate strand runs through Idaho National Laboratory's 'Prometheus' AI platform, integrated under a strategic partnership project announced 12 May 2026 in support of Pluto, Oklo's plutonium-fuelled reactor system under the Reactor Pilot Program.

relationships.note: Memorandum of understanding under which a monitoring room was commissioned for operator training.
relationships.context:
Announced 21 August 2025. The instrument is an MOU rather than a supply contract, and the deliverable described is a commissioned monitoring room supporting operator training.

It connects to Oklo's licensing strategy rather than to its plant equipment: the company is designing for a high degree of automation and has a Licensed Operator topical report before the NRC proposing that operators be licensed to the technology rather than to a single site, which would allow one control room to monitor several plants.
relationships.source: Oklo press release archive, 2025-08-21 (ABB memorandum of understanding; monitoring room commissioned for operator training)

policyExposure.exposure: The single most consequential policy instrument for Oklo. Executive Order 14301 directed DOE to approve at least three pilot reactors with a goal of criticality by 4 July 2026 and created the authorization pathway Aurora-INL, the Aurora Fuel Fabrication Facility and the Groves reactor are all using. Oklo and Atomic Alchemy were selected on 13 August 2025 for three of eleven projects. The FY2025 10-K states the pathway 'provides full authority to construct and operate the powerhouse'. Independent reporting notes the July 2026 goal was met — by Antares Nuclear, Valar Atomics and Deployable Energy, not by Oklo, whose reactor reached criticality on 5 August 2026.
policyExposure.mitigation: Oklo states it is 'currently working toward submitting an updated custom combined license application' to the NRC for commercial deployment, so the DOE pathway is described by the company as the route for first units rather than a permanent substitute.
policyExposure.source: ANS Nuclear Newswire — The deadline arrives: checking in on the Reactor Pilot Program (2026-07-02); Oklo FY2025 Form 10-K

policyExposure.exposure: Oklo submitted the first custom combined licence application for an advanced reactor on 17 March 2020; the NRC accepted it on 15 June 2020 and denied it without prejudice on 6 January 2022 for failure to supply sufficient information on maximum credible accident methodology, safety classification of structures, systems and components, and quality assurance scope. As of the Q2 2026 filing of 7 August 2026 no updated application has been submitted and the NRC's own pages list Oklo under pre-application activities only. Component approvals have advanced — a Principal Design Criteria topical report was approved on 6 May 2026 and a Licensed Operator topical report is under review — but there is no docketed reactor application. Independent reporting notes the Eielson Air Force Base contract is conditional on Oklo obtaining an NRC licence.
policyExposure.mitigation: Oklo states it is pursuing Part 52 rather than Part 50 because it designs, constructs and operates its own facilities, and is advancing topical reports so that a future application references pre-approved components.
policyExposure.source: NRC news release 22-002 (2022-01-06); NRC Oklo Aurora Powerhouse pre-application page (reviewed 2026-08-27); Oklo Q2 2026 Form 10-Q

policyExposure.exposure: The risk-informed, technology-inclusive licensing framework written for reactors that are not large light-water plants was voted final by the Commission on 26 March 2026 and published in the Federal Register on 30 March 2026, more than a year ahead of the statutory deadline. It creates an optional pathway suited to non-light-water designs. No Part 53 reference appears in Oklo's FY2025 10-K, which describes a Part 52 route.
policyExposure.source: Federal Register — Risk-Informed, Technology-Inclusive Regulatory Framework for Advanced Reactors (2026-03-30); ANS Nuclear Newswire

policyExposure.regime: HALEU supply and the DOE HALEU Availability Program
policyExposure.exposure: Oklo's first core comes from a 2019-2020 INL award of five metric tons of HALEU recovered from previously irradiated EBR-II fuel, and DOE retains ownership of that material. Independent reporting establishes the industry constraint: US HALEU enrichment is at pilot scale, with Centrus completing a 900 kg Phase 2 delivery in January 2026, and DOE's first HALEU allocation round in April 2025 went to TRISO-X, TerraPower, Kairos Power, Radiant and Westinghouse — not to Oklo. Oklo's commercial supply is a June 2026 letter of intent with Centrus for deliveries beginning in 2029, with price, volume and prepayment terms unnegotiated.
policyExposure.mitigation: The company states it is 'implementing a diversified fuel strategy' explicitly because 'the cost environment for various sources of fuel (including HALEU) has increased significantly in recent years' — the EBR-II stock, the Centrus letter of intent, the announced Tennessee recycling facility, and advanced negotiations under the DOE Surplus Plutonium Utilization Program.
policyExposure.source: PowerMag — DOE allocates first round of HALEU to five US advanced nuclear reactor developers (2025-04-09); Oklo FY2025 Form 10-K

policyExposure.exposure: Advanced nuclear remains eligible for the technology-neutral production and investment credits, and law-firm analyses of the One Big Beautiful Bill Act place the begin-construction condition before 2029 for the credits Oklo would use, with other summaries citing a longer window and a phase-out — the sources disagree and both readings are reported here. Aurora-INL began construction in September 2025 and is comfortably inside either window; Aurora-Ohio, with pre-construction slated to begin in 2026, sits closer to the earlier line. The Act also extended the energy-community bonus to areas with advanced-nuclear employment, which bears on the Piketon site. Section 45U, the zero-emission nuclear credit, applies to existing plants and does not apply to Oklo.
policyExposure.source: Clifford Chance — One Big Beautiful Bill Act: impacts on tax credits for nuclear (2025-07); Morgan Lewis — The impact of the OBBBA on nuclear tax incentives (2025-07)

policyExposure.exposure: PJM withdrew Oklo's Pike County interconnection request — 750 MW comprising 150 MW of advanced nuclear, 300 MW of fuel cells and 300 MW of natural gas — on 3 August 2026, stating that Oklo never demonstrated the project could ride through a sudden grid voltage drop. Oklo filed an emergency complaint at FERC on 28 August 2026, arguing PJM's rules were not designed for a multifuel project of this type and that PJM posted comments without issuing proper deficiency notices, and claiming a delay of at least 14 months and significantly increased development costs. Unresolved as of 4 September 2026.
policyExposure.source: Utility Dive — PJM drops Oklo advanced nuclear project from interconnection study cycle (published 2026-08-31, updated 2026-09-01)

policyExposure.exposure: Partial import restrictions with waivers run through 2027 and a complete ban applies from 2028; Russia imposed a retaliatory export ban on enriched uranium to the United States in November 2024. The Act unlocked a $2.72bn appropriation for domestic low-enriched and high-assay low-enriched uranium capacity. Oklo has no direct Russian supply exposure because its first core is domestic legacy material, but the Act tightens the industry-wide enrichment constraint described above and raises the strategic value of Centrus's Piketon capacity — the same site as Oklo's Ohio campus.
policyExposure.source: DOE Russian Uranium Ban waiver guidance; NRC backgrounder on the uranium import ban

financials.commentary: The financial record has to be read for what it is. Through 30 June 2026 Oklo has recognised $1.210M of revenue in its entire history, all of it in one quarter, all of it from engineering, consulting and fabrication services acquired in 2026, and none of it from selling power. Against that it carries $3.006B of cash and marketable securities, raised almost entirely through equity, and a 2026 spending plan of $520M to $650M. There is no order backlog in any accounting sense: the widely quoted 14 GW pipeline is a collection of non-binding letters of intent and one non-binding master agreement, and the company stopped publishing a pipeline figure after mid-2025. Expectations honesty: no genuine published consensus was found for Q3 2024, and the vendor disagreement on Q1 2026 is real enough that the beat-or-miss verdict is not resolvable — both are stated rather than smoothed. Market data for context, as of the close on 3 September 2026: share price $39.84, market capitalisation $7.41B, short interest around 17% of float, and analyst price targets spanning $14 to $130 across 25 analysts — roughly a tenfold spread, which is the market's own statement about how binary the outcome is.

strategyRead: 1. **(High confidence)** We assess that Oklo's decisive strategic move was regulatory rather than technical: routing its first reactors onto the DOE authorization pathway created by Executive Order 14301 rather than waiting for an NRC licence. Basis: the 2020 combined licence application was denied without prejudice in January 2022 for failure to supply information; no updated application had been submitted as of the 7 August 2026 filing; and Aurora-INL, the fuel fabrication facility and the Groves reactor are all proceeding under DOE Other Transaction Agreements and safety-analysis approvals. Groves went from groundbreaking to criticality in about eleven months on that pathway. The judgement's limit is equally clear — the Eielson Air Force Base award is reported as conditional on an NRC licence Oklo does not hold, so the DOE route buys first units and not the commercial fleet.

2. **(High confidence)** We assess the customer book should be read as a pipeline of options rather than an order book. Basis: not one definitive power purchase agreement appears anywhere in the company's public record. The Switch instrument is explicitly a non-binding master agreement; Diamondback, Prometheus Hyperscale and Equinix are non-binding letters of intent; Eielson is a notice of intent to award; the Meta agreement is a prepayment structure that is not described as a PPA. The only binding commercial contract Oklo has announced is with a supplier, Siemens Energy. Oklo's own funnel description — MOU, then site scoping, then LOI, then PPA before construction begins — places every announced counterparty short of the last step.

3. **(Moderate confidence)** We assess vertical integration into fuel is a genuine strategic differentiator rather than scope creep, because the binding constraint on the whole advanced-reactor sector is fuel rather than reactors. Basis: US HALEU enrichment is at pilot scale; DOE's first allocation round in April 2025 went to five developers not including Oklo; Oklo's own first core is a fixed five metric tons of government-owned legacy EBR-II material; and its commercial supply is a letter of intent for deliveries starting in 2029 whose price and volume are unnegotiated. The company's largest announced capital commitment — up to $1.68bn — is a fuel recycling facility, not a power plant. The confidence is moderate because none of the fuel programme has produced fuel yet.

4. **(Moderate confidence)** We assess the acquisition programme is a supply-chain hedge on the narrowest bottlenecks rather than diversification. Basis: Creative Engineers brings alkali-metal systems including sodium components, which is precisely the speciality a sodium-cooled reactor cannot buy freely; ARMEC brings manufacturing and prototyping; Atomic Alchemy brought a reactor programme that could reach criticality on a shorter clock than the Aurora. That last one has already paid: Oklo can point to an operating reactor and a granted NRC licence, both of which are true and neither of which involves an Aurora.

5. **(Moderate confidence)** We assess the equity-funded model is the strategy, not merely its financing. Basis: roughly $3.0bn of cash and securities against $84.3M of total liabilities and no convertible debt, raised through a SPAC and three at-the-market programmes, with about 15% dilution in the first half of 2026 alone. A build-own-operate developer with no revenue must fund construction from somewhere, and Oklo has chosen shareholders over lenders. Two consequences follow: the share price is an input to the business rather than an output of it, and the company has no DOE loan — its own chief executive has publicly criticised the loan programme office as designed for large conventional reactors.

6. **(Low confidence)** We assess the interconnection queue, not the reactor and not the licence, may prove the binding constraint on the Ohio campus. Basis: PJM withdrew the 750 MW Pike County project on 3 August 2026 for failure to demonstrate voltage ride-through; Oklo filed an emergency complaint at FERC on 28 August claiming at least 14 months of delay; the matter is unresolved. Confidence is low because the dispute is live and the outcome unknown, but the shape of it is familiar from every utility dossier in this corpus — the study process, not the equipment, sets the date.

7. **(Low confidence)** We assess that the gap between the announced pipeline and the delivered plant is now large enough to be a strategic risk in itself. Basis: an order book quoted at 14 GW in mid-2025 and no longer quoted at all; a single non-binding instrument accounting for roughly six sevenths of it; a share price down some 70% from its peak with short interest around 17%; analyst targets spanning $14 to $130; and a 2024 short report whose central factual claims — no NRC-approved design, no meaningful revenue — remain accurate two years later. Collection gap: no independent model of Oklo's levelised cost or capital cost per kilowatt exists in the public record, and Oklo's own unit economics date from 2023, describe a 15 MWe machine rather than the 75 MWe lead unit, and have never been reaffirmed.
